facts.fact: Equatorial Guinea is listed among the 49 countries that signed the Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence, done at Kigali on 4 April 2025 alongside the African Union and Smart Africa.

Equatorial Guinea was one of six countries whose delegations took part in the Second Lusophone Africa Data Governance Workshop in Luanda, 15-17 June 2026, hosted by Angola's data protection agency with Smart Africa, the World Bank, CETIC.br and UNESCO; the UNESCO article is dated 2026-07-28.

Equatorial Guinea signed the non-binding CPLP Charter of Rights and Principles in Digital Environments at Sao Tome on 19 July 2024, through its ambassador and permanent representative to the CPLP, alongside the other member states (six of the nine are African).

note: A national telecom plan was pitched to the World Bank, which is not an African body; the CEMAC and CEEAC digital market is only an aim.
Preparation-stage World Bank program plan (appraisal Nov 2026, financing not approved); states no delivered system, rule, figure or survey for this study.

facts.fact: Equatorial Guinea currently chairs the rotating ECCAS presidency, and its Director General of Telecommunications, Celedonio Nguema Angono, spoke for it at the 19-20 October 2026 Brazzaville validation of the ECCAS Regional Data Governance Framework.

Equatorial Guinea was elected to chair the UN Statistical Commission for Africa (StatCom-Africa) for 2026-2028 at its tenth session in Addis Ababa, 19-23 October 2026, INEGE's director-general presiding, per INEGE; the agenda includes data as an economic asset and AI regulation in the public sector.

note: The roaming memorandums between CEMAC regulators date from November 2021, outside the three-year window; the 2025 accords are not yet signed; no membership of a digital policy body is stated.
A Gabon roaming agreement appears only as a related-link headline, not in the article text.

facts.fact: The Cameroon regulator (ART) names Equatorial Guinea as one of eight member states of ARTAC.
